devsecops_security_workflow.overview: This workflow implements a comprehensive 5-stage DevSecOps security control model designed for regulated banking environments. The approach ensures TLS/mTLS/OAuth security through layered control points across the entire software delivery lifecycle, from development through production runtime.

principle.name: control_based_security
principle.description: Security assurance is achieved through multiple complementary control points rather than relying on a single tool or scanner.

principle.name: verification_over_assumption
principle.description: Never assume security configurations are correct. Always verify through multiple stages: static analysis, build-time inspection, deployment validation, and runtime verification.

principle.name: eliminate_hidden_risks
principle.description: Modern frameworks abstract security complexity (Spring Boot SSL bundles, OAuth auto-configuration, templated infrastructure). Make these abstractions visible and verifiable at each lifecycle stage.

principle.name: continuous_compliance
principle.description: Security is not a one-time activity. Continuously monitor for drift, certificate expiration, and cryptographic changes.

stage.name: shift_left_detection
stage.title: Shift-Left Detection: Early Identification of Security Abstractions
stage.objective: Identify risky security abstractions and misconfigurations during development before they reach deployment.
stage.when_to_execute: - During local development (pre-commit hooks) - In pull request validation - Early CI/CD pipeline stages

activity.name: static_code_analysis
activity.description: Use custom Semgrep rules to detect security abstractions

targets.target: Spring Boot ssl.fromBundle() usage for mTLS
OAuth login flow activation without explicit constraints
TLS configuration through external property files

activity.action: Flag areas requiring verification and governance review

targets.target: nginx configuration files for TLS hardening

activity.name: secrets_detection
activity.description: Prevent accidental exposure of sensitive cryptographic material

outputs.output: List of flagged security abstractions requiring review
IaC security findings with severity ratings
Traceable findings for security team review

success_criteria.criterion: All high-severity findings addressed before merge

stage.name: cryptographic_visibility
stage.title: Cryptographic Visibility: Build-Time Algorithm Analysis
stage.objective: Provide comprehensive visibility into cryptographic algorithms, libraries, and protocols used across the application and its dependencies.
stage.when_to_execute: - During CI/CD build process - After dependency resolution - Before artifact creation

activity.name: quantum_safe_explorer_integration
activity.description: Integrate IBM Quantum Safe Explorer for cryptographic inventory

capabilities.capability: Inventory all cryptographic algorithms in use
Detect TLS stacks (OpenSSL, BoringSSL, Java security providers)
Map protocol usage (TLS versions, cipher suites)

activity.name: cryptographic_policy_enforcement

policy_checks.check: No use of MD5 or SHA-1 for security purposes
Minimum RSA key size of 2048 bits (prefer 3072+)

activity.action: Block builds that violate cryptographic policies

outputs.output: Quantum risk assessment with migration recommendations
Build gate decisions (pass/fail based on policy)

success_criteria.criterion: All cryptographic usage documented and approved
No policy violations in production builds
Quantum risk exposure understood and tracked

stage.name: deployment_validation
stage.title: Deployment Validation: Configuration Resolution Verification
stage.objective: Validate that templated configurations resolve correctly and meet security standards when deployed to target environments.
stage.when_to_execute: - Immediately before deployment - After configuration template resolution - During deployment pipeline execution

activity.name: configuration_resolution_validation
activity.description: Verify resolved configurations match security requirements

validation_targets.target: Ansible variable resolution for TLS settings
Certificate path resolution and file existence
Kubernetes secret mounting and volume configuration

validation_checks.check: Certificate files exist and are readable
Cipher suites are from approved list

activity.name: pre_deployment_security_scan
activity.description: Scan final deployment artifacts for security issues

activity.name: configuration_drift_prevention
activity.description: Ensure deployed configuration matches approved baseline

outputs.output: Deployment validation report with pass/fail status
Resolved configuration files for audit trail

success_criteria.criterion: Certificates are valid and properly configured
No drift from approved security baseline

stage.name: runtime_verification
stage.title: Runtime Verification: Live Security Posture Validation
stage.objective: Verify the actual security posture exposed to clients and counterparties by testing live endpoints and authentication flows.
stage.when_to_execute: - Immediately after deployment - During smoke testing phase - As part of continuous security monitoring

activity.name: tls_endpoint_validation
activity.description: Actively scan TLS endpoints to verify configuration

validation_checks.check: Only approved TLS versions are enabled
Only approved cipher suites are offered

activity.name: mtls_validation
activity.description: Verify mutual TLS authentication is properly configured

activity.name: oauth_flow_validation
activity.description: Test OAuth 2.0 authentication flows for security issues

validation_checks.check: PKCE is used for public clients

outputs.output: TLS endpoint scan results with findings

success_criteria.criterion: All TLS endpoints meet security standards
OAuth flows are secure and properly configured

remediation_triggers.trigger: High-severity findings require remediation within 24 hours
Medium findings tracked for next deployment cycle

stage.name: continuous_compliance
stage.title: Continuous Compliance: Ongoing Monitoring and Drift Detection
stage.objective: Maintain security assurance over time through continuous monitoring, detecting configuration drift, certificate expiration, and cryptographic changes.
stage.when_to_execute: - Continuously in production - Scheduled periodic scans - Triggered by configuration changes

activity.name: continuous_tls_monitoring
activity.description: Monitor TLS posture for changes and degradation

alerting.alert: TLS vulnerability discovered in deployed version

guideline.name: iterative_improvement
guideline.description: Implement controls iteratively. Start with critical controls (runtime validation) and expand coverage over time. Don't wait for perfect implementation.

guideline.name: evidence_generation
guideline.description: Every control point must generate traceable evidence. This evidence supports audit requirements and demonstrates due diligence.

guideline.name: automation_first
guideline.description: Automate all controls wherever possible. Manual processes don't scale and introduce human error. Use CI/CD integration extensively.

guideline.name: fail_secure
guideline.description: When controls detect issues, default to blocking deployment or triggering alerts. Never silently ignore security findings.

guideline.name: defense_in_depth
guideline.description: Multiple control stages provide redundancy. If one stage misses an issue, subsequent stages should catch it. Never rely on a single control point.

integration.name: cicd_pipeline
integration.description: Embed security controls into existing CI/CD pipelines

stages.stage: Pre-commit: Static analysis and secrets detection
Build: Cryptographic visibility and policy enforcement

integration.name: incident_response
integration.description: Security findings feed into incident response processes

integration.name: risk_management
integration.description: Control effectiveness maps to risk statements
